title: RTX 5090 Price for AI: Rent vs Buy (November 2026)
summary: RTX 5090 pricing: rent from $0.78/GPU-hr on demand, or buy for $6,199 to $11,896 in November 2026, three to six times the $1,999 MSRP. See the breakeven.
body_markdown:
**Only a few providers rent RTX 5090 GPUs, and it costs $0.78-$1.19/GPU-hr on demand.** Buying one costs $6,199-$11,896 in November 2026, 3-6x its $1,999 MSRP. At those prices, renting is cheaper for most AI workloads. Buying only pays off for a card that runs most of the day for years.


This guide covers RTX 5090 cloud rental prices, street prices, buy-vs-rent payback and what fits in 32 GB of VRAM. The pricing information is reviewed weekly.


**Takeaways**


- **RTX 5090 rental costs start at $0.78/hr** (Vast.ai).
- **RTX 5090 retail cards sell for $6,199-$11,896** .
- **A $6,199 RTX 5090** takes about 1.1 years of 24/7 use to beat renting.
- **Thunder Compute offers the RTX A6000 at $0.35/hr** .

## RTX 5090 Price to Buy


Buying an RTX 5090 costs[$6,199](https://www.newegg.com/asus-rog-astral-rog-astral-rtx5090-p32g-edition20-geforce-rtx-5090-32gb-video-card-triple-fans/p/N82E16814126846) to[$11,896](https://www.newegg.com/asus-rog-astral-rog-astral-rtx5090-p32g-edition20-geforce-rtx-5090-32gb-video-card-triple-fans/p/N82E16814126843?Item=9SIBYT0M6M8389) at US retail listings checked on November 10, 2026. NVIDIA set a[launch MSRP of $1,999](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-blackwell-geforce-rtx-50-series-opens-new-world-of-ai-computer-graphics) . The Founders Edition (NVIDIA's own reference card) is listed at $1,999 on[NVIDIA's marketplace](https://marketplace.nvidia.com/en-us/consumer/graphics-cards/?gpu=RTX+5090) but is out of stock.

### Buy vs Rent an RTX 5090 for AI Workloads


Renting an RTX 5090 is cheaper than buying one at November 2026 street prices, unless the card runs close to 24/7. The payback comparison uses the $0.78/hr Vast.ai median as the rental price. It counts electricity at about $0.10/hr (a 0.8 kW system at $0.13/kWh). It excludes the rest of the PC, cooling and depreciation, so real payback periods are longer.

## RTX 5090 vs RTX 4090


The RTX 5090 has 8 GB more VRAM than the RTX 4090 and[about 1.8x its memory bandwidth](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/graphics-cards/compare/) . Memory bandwidth usually limits LLM generation speed, so the RTX 5090's lead matters most for inference. The RTX 5090 also draws 125 W more than the RTX 4090.

### When to Choose the RTX 5090


Choose the RTX 5090 when your model needs 24-32 GB, or when tokens/second matter for serving. FP4 support can also speed up inference in runtimes and models that use FP4. If your workload isn't bandwidth-bound,[Thunder Compute's RTX A6000](https://www.thundercompute.com/blog/nvidia-rtx-a6000-pricing) runs it with 48 GB of VRAM. At $0.35/hr, the RTX A6000 costs less than half the RTX 5090 median.


### When to Choose a 48 to 80 GB GPU Instead


Choose a 48-80 GB data-center GPU when the RTX 5090's 32 GB runs out. Common cases include:


- 70B-class models
- Long context windows
- Larger batch sizes
- Full fine-tuning


Splitting a model across several RTX 5090s works, but slows multi-GPU jobs. The RTX 5090 lacks NVLink (NVIDIA's GPU-to-GPU interconnect), so the cards communicate over PCIe.


> [Launch an RTX A6000 (48 GB) on Thunder Compute at $0.35/hr.](https://www.thundercompute.com/pricing)


## What LLMs Fit in RTX 5090 VRAM?


An RTX 5090 fits LLMs up to about 30B-40B parameters at 4-bit, or about 8B-13B at 16-bit. The VRAM figures in the model table cover weights only. The KV cache and activations need several more GB, depending on context length and batch size.

## Last Thoughts on RTX 5090 Pricing


Renting an RTX 5090 at $0.78-$1.19/hr beats buying one for almost every workload that doesn't run 24/7. For more than 32 GB, Thunder Compute offers the 48 GB RTX A6000 ($0.35/hr) and A100 80GB ($1.09/hr).


## FAQ


### How Much Does It Cost to Rent an RTX 5090?


An RTX 5090 rents for $0.78/GPU-hr at the Vast.ai median and $1.19/GPU-hr on Runpod, as of November 10, 2026. Vast.ai hosts range from $0.49-$1.12/hr. At the Vast.ai median, running one 24/7 costs about $566/month.


### How Much Does an RTX 5090 Cost to Buy Right Now?


An RTX 5090 costs $6,199-$11,896 at US retail listings in November 2026. That is 3-6x the $1,999 launch MSRP.


### Why Is the RTX 5090 So Expensive in 2026?


The $1,999 MSRP only applies to the Founders Edition, which is out of stock on NVIDIA's marketplace as of November 2026. Partner cards from retailers and resellers are listed at $6,199-$11,896, the real cost of buying an RTX 5090.


### Is It Cheaper to Rent or Buy an RTX 5090 for AI?


Renting is cheaper unless the RTX 5090 runs most of the day. A $6,199 card pays for itself in about 1.1 years at 24/7 use, or 3.2 years at 8h/day. That estimate uses the $0.78/hr Vast.ai median and includes electricity, but not the rest of the PC.


### What Are the RTX 5090's Specs?


The RTX 5090 is a Blackwell GPU with 32 GB of GDDR7, 1,792 GB/s of memory bandwidth and 21,760 CUDA cores. It delivers 419 TFLOPS of dense FP16 tensor throughput and draws 575 W.
